posts.name: Five signs your month-end close is too slow
posts.excerpt: If the numbers arrive after the decisions, the close is too slow. Here is how to tell, and what to fix first.
posts.content:
A close that takes three weeks means every decision in that month is made on old numbers.

1. Reports arrive after the meeting

If the board pack is late, the close is the bottleneck.

2. The same corrections every month

Recurring journals are a sign the process, not the people, needs work.

3. One person holds it together

A close that depends on one person is a risk, not a process.

posts.name: What an operations review actually looks at
posts.excerpt: Two weeks, eight interviews and a ranked list. A look inside the review we run most often.
posts.content:
An operations review is not an audit. It follows the work, not the org chart.

The interviews

We talk to the people who do the work, not only the people who manage it.

The list

Every finding gets a cost, a fix and an owner.
